|        - |    39 | `/*` |
|        - |    40 | ` * The code in this file implements execution method of the PH7 Virtual Machine.` |
|        - |    41 | ` * The PH7 compiler (implemented in 'compiler.c' and 'parse.c') generates a bytecode program` |
|        - |    42 | ` * which is then executed by the virtual machine implemented here to do the work of the PHP` |
|        - |    43 | ` * statements.` |
|        - |    44 | ` * PH7 bytecode programs are similar in form to assembly language. The program consists` |
|        - |    45 | ` * of a linear sequence of operations .Each operation has an opcode and 3 operands.` |
|        - |    46 | ` * Operands P1 and P2 are integers where the first is signed while the second is unsigned.` |
|        - |    47 | ` * Operand P3 is an arbitrary pointer specific to each instruction. The P2 operand is usually` |
|        - |    48 | ` * the jump destination used by the OP_JMP,OP_JZ,OP_JNZ,... instructions.` |
|        - |    49 | ` * Opcodes will typically ignore one or more operands. Many opcodes ignore all three operands.` |
|        - |    50 | ` * Computation results are stored on a stack. Each entry on the stack is of type ph7_value.` |
|        - |    51 | ` * PH7 uses the ph7_value object to represent all values that can be stored in a PHP variable.` |
|        - |    52 | ` * Since PHP uses dynamic typing for the values it stores. Values stored in ph7_value objects` |
|        - |    53 | ` * can be integers,floating point values,strings,arrays,class instances (object in the PHP jargon)` |
|        - |    54 | ` * and so on.` |
|        - |    55 | ` * Internally,the PH7 virtual machine manipulates nearly all PHP values as ph7_values structures.` |
|        - |    56 | ` * Each ph7_value may cache multiple representations(string,integer etc.) of the same value.` |
|        - |    57 | ` * An implicit conversion from one type to the other occurs as necessary.` |
|        - |    58 | ` * Most of the code in this file is taken up by the [VmByteCodeExec()] function which does` |
|        - |    59 | ` * the work of interpreting a PH7 bytecode program. But other routines are also provided` |
|        - |    60 | ` * to help in building up a program instruction by instruction. Also note that sepcial` |
|        - |    61 | ` * functions that need access to the underlying virtual machine details such as [die()],` |
|        - |    62 | ` * [func_get_args()],[call_user_func()],[ob_start()] and many more are implemented here.` |
|        - |    63 | ` */` |

|        - |  2759 | `/*` |
|        - |  2760 | ` * Static operand-stack depth analysis (BYTECODE.md stage 7).` |
|        - |  2761 | ` *` |
|        - |  2762 | ` * The safe upper bound on a body's operand-stack depth is its instruction count` |
|        - |  2763 | ` * (no instruction pushes more than one net slot), and that is what` |
|        - |  2764 | ` * VmNewOperandStack allocates by default. For DEEP recursion that over-allocates` |
|        - |  2765 | ` * badly — one operand stack per live frame, each sized to the whole body — so` |
|        - |  2766 | ` * this pass computes a TIGHT bound (typically single digits) for the common` |
|        - |  2767 | ` * shape of a recursive function, letting the OP_CALL path allocate small stacks.` |
|        - |  2768 | ` *` |
|        - |  2769 | ` * Undersizing an operand stack is a heap overflow, so the analysis is` |
|        - |  2770 | ` * conservative BY CONSTRUCTION:` |
|        - |  2771 | ` *   - Every modeled opcode uses pushmax = 1 (the engine invariant) and a popmin` |
|        - |  2772 | ` *     that never exceeds its real pop on any path (verified per handler). Over-` |
|        - |  2773 | ` *     estimating height is safe; the only unsafe direction — over-crediting a` |
|        - |  2774 | ` *     pop — makes height go negative, which triggers fallback.` |
|        - |  2775 | ` *   - A body is sized by this analysis only if EVERY instruction is in the` |
|        - |  2776 | ` *     verified modeled set (VmInstrStackEffect). Any other opcode (try/catch,` |
|        - |  2777 | ` *     yield, foreach, switch/match, spread, string/array builders, …) returns` |
|        - |  2778 | ` *     VM_STACK_UNMODELED for the whole body -> caller keeps the instruction-count` |
|        - |  2779 | ` *     bound. There is no partial/unsafe middle.` |
|        - |  2780 | ` *   - Control flow follows real edges (JMP/JZ/JNZ + the fused comparison-branch` |
|        - |  2781 | ` *     forms). An out-of-range jump, a negative height, or a height exceeding the` |
|        - |  2782 | ` *     instruction-count bound -> fallback.` |
|        - |  2783 | ` *   - VM_STACK_GUARD slack is still added by the operand-stack allocator on top` |
|        - |  2784 | ` *     of the returned depth, and the full corpus runs under ASan (which catches` |
|        - |  2785 | ` *     any undersize as a heap-buffer-overflow) as the standing validation.` |
|        - |  2786 | ` *` |
|        - |  2787 | `` * The exception-resume `pc =` reassignments inside some modeled handlers`` |
|        - |  2788 | ` * (STORE/CALL/DONE/comparisons) only fire when this activation OWNS a catch` |
|        - |  2789 | ` * frame — impossible in a modeled body, since OP_LOAD_EXCEPTION is unmodeled and` |
|        - |  2790 | ` * forces fallback — so they are dead in analyzed bodies and need no edge.` |
|        - |  2791 | ` *` |
|        - |  2792 | ` * Drift safety (for whoever adds an opcode or changes a handler's stack effect):` |
|        - |  2793 | ` * VmInstrStackEffect is a hand-maintained model that must stay in sync with the` |
|        - |  2794 | ` * real handlers. Two things keep a drift from becoming a silent undersize: a NEW` |
|        - |  2795 | `` * opcode is unmodeled by default (its `default:` return forces the safe`` |
|        - |  2796 | ` * instruction-count bound), so only *changing a modeled opcode's real pop count*` |
|        - |  2797 | ` * to exceed its popmin can undersize — and that is caught deterministically by` |
|        - |  2798 | ` * the standing ASan-over-corpus run (an undersize is a heap-buffer-overflow on` |
|        - |  2799 | ` * the operand stack). When touching a modeled handler's push/pop, re-check its` |
